study_identification_part.si4_title: Normative modelling of brain function abnormalities in complex pathology needs the whole brain

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states objectives: introduce a whole-brain normative modeling approach (FUNCOIN) for rsfMRI functional connectivity, build a normative model using a large healthy cohort, and evaluate its ability to detect deviations in clinical cohorts (BD, PD), including assessing out-of-sample performance and clinical relevance.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "we here argue that ... whole-brain normative models are more suitable ... we thus propose Functional Connectivity Integrative Normative Modelling (FUNCOIN) ... Using FUNCOIN and UK Biobank resting-state fMRI data ... we found that subjects with bipolar disorder and Parkinson's disease were significantly ... more likely ... to exhibit abnormal FC patterns"; "we create an integrative normative model of FC from 32000 individuals and test it on 14000 healthy subjects"

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: NEW model: Eligibility criteria for healthy reference cohort are described (no ICD-10 F/G diagnoses in UKB). Final sample sizes for training (N=32,000) and test (N=14,000) are reported. However, explicit image quality standards and reasons for exclusion are not detailed.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we consider a subject healthy if they have no psychiatric or neurological diagnoses (group F or G diagnoses in ICD-10) ... We divide the subjects into three groups ... training data, N=32,000 ... test data, N=14,000"

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are core covariates. The model includes sex, age, and sex–age interaction. Multi-site data are addressed by exploring scanning site as an additional covariate and showing minimal impact on the first two components.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "We included sex, age, and sex-age interaction as covariates ... The data come from 4 different scanning sites ... scanning site was included as an additive, categorical variable ..."; "This led to the same γ1, γ2 ... focusing on components unaffected by the choice of site (as in this study)."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source is clearly specified as UK Biobank with citation and description of dataset scale and parcellation.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We use rsfMRI data from UKB (N>60,000 people)"; "The data consist of rsfMRI time series in the UKB-parcellation with 55 components from independent component analysis (ICA)."

Per guidance, when using preprocessed data from existing projects with no added preprocessing, answer NA.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "The data consist of rsfMRI time series in the UKB-parcellation with 55 components ... Our measure of brain function is FC, determined ... as the Pearson correlation matrix"

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: A hold-out validation strategy is used: model fitting on 32,000 training subjects and out-of-sample assessment on 14,000 healthy test subjects.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We divide the subjects into three groups ... training data, N=32,000 ... test data, N=14,000"; "With the out-of-sample healthy test subjects, we assess explanatory power and generalizability of the model"

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model is trained and evaluated within UK Biobank partitions. No application to an independent external healthy dataset beyond UKB is reported.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No mention of an external healthy dataset beyond the UKB training/test split; validation described as "out-of-sample healthy test subjects" within UKB.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described in detail: an adaptation of covariate-assisted principal regression with a log-linear model on FC projections, bias-correction step, component selection rationale, and available implementation as a Python package (FUNCOIN).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "we introduce FUNCOIN ... an adaptation of ... covariate-assisted principal regression ... finds FC components ... whose magnitude maximally depend on sex and age ... log-linear model"; "After ... identify projections ... we perform linear regression on the transformed FC values to get unbiased beta estimates ... This modified, unbiased version ... is FUNCOIN."; "a python package, 'FUNCOIN', is released ... installable ... with pip"

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model fit is quantified via R^2 for the linear relationships between FC projections and covariates (R^2=0.32 and 0.24). Calibration aspects are referenced (healthy Z-scores conform to expected standard normal), indicating assessment of distributional fit, though detailed coverage metrics are not exhaustively reported in main text.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "the first projection is associated with both sex and age (Fig. 2A, top, R^2=0.32), and the second projection is associated mostly with sex (Fig. 2A, bottom, R^2=0.24)."; "Given that the healthy population Z-scores follow a standard normal distribution (see model validation below)..."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Partition sample sizes for training and test sets are reported. Demographic characteristics per partition are shown qualitatively (sex-stratified plots), but detailed tabulated demographics per partition are not provided.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "training data, N=32,000 ... test data, N=14,000"; "For each sex (females red, males blue), the normative graphs ... 100 random out-of-sample subjects for each sex are plotted (black)"
